Nice and simple — quick rules of thumb to decide delete vs tuck away (archive/folder):

- Actionable now? Keep until you finish the action, then delete unless it’s a record you’ll need.
- Is it a record (tax, contract, invoice, pay stub, legal, warranty)? Tuck it away — these are worth keeping.
- Time-limited (boarding pass, one-time code, event confirmation)? Delete after it’s expired/used.
- Is it needed for an ongoing project or thread you’ll return to soon? Keep in a project folder; delete when the project ends.
- Can it be easily recreated or found online (terms of service, promo you can look up)? Delete.
- Receipts: keep only what you need for returns/taxes — delete the rest.
- Newsletters, promos, deal emails: delete unless you genuinely read them; unsubscribe instead.
- Sentimental stuff (cards, personal notes): consider exporting/save to a memories folder, otherwise delete to avoid clutter.
- Large attachments you’ve saved elsewhere (photos, PDFs): delete the email after saving the attachment.
- Unsure? Set short retention (30–90 days) and auto-delete/archive after that.

Use two places: “Important/Records” folder for things you must keep, and “Archive/Projects” for stuff you might reference. Everything else — if it isn’t actionable, irreplaceable, or required by law — delete.
